clauses.reason: Terminated by its own terms at the close of Tuesday, December 31, 1935, the second of the two half-day closings ('at 1 P.M. on Tuesday, December 24, 1935 ... and at 1 P.M. on Tuesday, December 31, 1935'). Actor: EO 7249 itself. The dossier's only own-terms record is the undated shift condition, so the end cites the order's complete registered text, which contains the stated dates.

research_rationale:
EO 7249 (December 12, 1935, Franklin D. Roosevelt). Text and identity: read in full in the registered American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts; grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-10-28: the APP page record with the same sha256 in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl has a heading naming EO 7249, its date (December 12, 1935) appears in the held text, and its text_sha256 equals the held file's. Clauses are quoted from that registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy. It closes the executive departments, independent establishments and other agencies in the District of Columbia, including the Government Printing Office and the Navy Yard and stations, at 1 P.M. on Tuesday, December 24, 1935 and at 1 P.M. on Tuesday, December 31, 1935, and excuses employees in the District and in the field service from duty at those hours, except those excluded by their agency heads for special public reasons or whose absence would be inconsistent with existing law. A second paragraph applies the order to shift workers, who are excused 'after four hours of work on the dates specified'. Identity: number, date and subject agree across the APP page, the census register (1935-12-12) and the WPA 1944 list ('Federal offices ordered closed at 1 p. m. on Dec. 24 and 31, 1935'). The type label office_closing_mourning fits. First end: by its own terms at the close of 1935-12-31, the second and last day it governs (the December 24 part was spent at the close of that day). Both days were Tuesdays, as the order says. The dossier's own-terms record for the shift paragraph is classed as a condition with no date; the condition is tied to 'the dates specified' and adds no later date. Searches on 2026-10-28: the WPA 1944 list and census titles for Christmas and late-December closings 1931-1936 (EO 7499 of November 27, 1936, for December 24 and 26, 1936, is a new order for another year and does not name EO 7249), and a citation search of every held order text for 'Order No. 7249' (only navigation links in Wikisource pages for adjacent numbers); nothing names EO 7249.
